text:
Sam (AE): Prospect wants BYOK via customer CloudHSM, FIPS 140-2 L3, and a clear procurement cost breakdown. Need a simple POC runbook + a stub SOW line items.
Ivy (Solutions Eng): I'll put together a lean POC: encrypt/decrypt, alias rotation, and fallback demo.
Marco (Security): Quick security constraints: must forward CloudTrail KMS events to their logging account; require kms key policy that explicitly denies ScheduleKeyDeletion except via approved SOW process; prefer Condition on aws:SourceVpc for usage.
Ellen (SRE): For Private deployment we need VPC peering/VPN details or Transit GW, and an IAM role ARN for our service principal. If they insist no key material leaves their account, Hosted is not viable.
Sam (AE): Pricing question: do we charge per HSM-backed CMK monthly? Prospect will push procurement on that.
Ellen (SRE): Typical approach: if CloudHSM is in their account we pass through their AWS CloudHSM cost and add a one-time integration SOW fee + small recurring ops fee for Private hosting. Hosted customers using our managed keys see no per-CMK bill. I'll draft numbers after scoping.
Ivy (Solutions Eng): Draft POC runbook (short):
1) Customer creates an HSM-backed CMK in their AWS account and tags it for the POC.
2) Customer adds a Key Policy or creates a KMS grant to allow Redwood's service role: Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey.
3) Provide CMK ARN and an assumable IAM role or grant token.
4) Run encrypt/decrypt tests via Redwood API; measure p95/p99 KMS call latency.
5) Execute rotation: rotate alias to new key and validate decryption of prior ciphertext (rewrap if they requested).
6) Revoke grant to simulate failure and show demo fallback to non-HSM demo key (not for production).
Marco (Security): Add: require CloudTrail log forwarding, set alert for repeated kms:Decrypt failures, and document key ceremony steps for split-knowledge if they want on-prem HSM.
Sam (AE): Contract-wise they want to know about escrow/backup of keys and whether Redwood ever holds key material.
Marco (Security): Official answer: Redwood does not persist customer CMK material for BYOK CloudHSM flows. Escrow or copies are only done if expressly contracted and documented in SOW with approved controls. Backups of CMKs are handled by their KMS provider (AWS).
Ivy (Solutions Eng): Small sample key policy to give them (they must adapt ARNs):
{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::REDACTED:role/redwood-service"},"Action":["kms:Encrypt","kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey"],"Resource":"*","Condition":{"StringEquals":{"aws:SourceAccount":"123456789012"}}}]}
Marco (Security): Also recommend explicit Deny for kms:ScheduleKeyDeletion and require kms:GrantIsForAWSService only when using grants.
Sam (AE): Timeline: they want kickoff in three weeks. What's realistic for Private + CloudHSM BYOK?
Ellen (SRE): If they provide account access, peering, and a security contact quickly: 4-6 weeks for Private+CloudHSM integration. On-prem HSM adds lead time for procurement and ceremonies (8-12 weeks).
Sam (AE): I'll need a procurement stub: please include pass-through HSM cost, integration SOW, and recurring ops line.
Ellen (SRE): Stub example: "CloudHSM pass-through: customer-billed to their AWS account; Integration SOW: one-time $Z for network/config/cert validation; Private ops: recurring $W/month for dedicated support and HSM monitoring." I'll convert to numbers in the SOW ticket.
contract-bot: Created ticket SOW-7821 for "CloudHSM cost stub and POC runbook".
Ivy (Solutions Eng): I'll produce the one-page POC and test payloads. ETA tomorrow EOD.
Marco (Security): I'll compile the questionnaire responses and flag any items needing legal review.
Sam (AE): Thanks folks. I'll collect the pack and schedule the kickoff once we have numbers. :thumbsup:
